Full‑time employees with 3–5 years of service accrue **20 days of PTO per year** (160 hours), which translates to about **6.67 hours per pay period** (24 pay periods per year).  
(POL‑PTO‑001 §2.1 Accrual Rates)

Helios observes a different set of paid holidays for each office location.  
- **United States offices**: 12 paid holidays (e.g., New Year’s Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas, etc.) — see POL‑HOL‑001 §2.1.  
- **Singapore (APAC) office**: 11 paid public holidays (e.g., Chinese New Year, Good Friday, Hari Raya Puasa, etc.) — see POL‑HOL‑001 §2.3.  

Employees receive the holiday schedule of their **assigned office location** (POL‑HOL‑001 §5), so the holidays are not the same across all offices.

You may work from another country for **up to 30 calendar days in a rolling 12‑month period**.  
That 30‑day limit applies across all countries combined. In addition, the policy lists specific country limits: for example, 21 consecutive days in Spain, Italy, Germany, Netherlands, and 14 days in Mexico and Japan.  

(POL‑INTL‑001 §2 The 30‑Day Rule)

**No — the request fails on two independent grounds.**

1. **Insufficient balance** — Jonas has 13 hours (1.62 days) available, but the request is 24 hours (3 days). Shortfall: **11 hours** (POL-PTO-001 §3.3 Insufficient Balance).
2. **Insufficient notice** — 3 consecutive business days requires **10 business days** notice; only **6 business days** are given (today 2026-09-12 → 2026-09-21) (POL-PTO-001 §3.1 Notice Requirements).

The blackout check passes — no blackout period applies to Customer Support for these dates (POL-PTO-001 §4 Blackout Periods).

**Compliant alternatives:**
- **Shorten the request** to at most 1.5 days (13 hours) of PTO — this fixes the balance issue, but the notice rule still applies to the length requested.
- **Move the start date later** to meet the 10-business-day notice requirement. For 3 consecutive business days, the earliest compliant start is **2026-09-25** (10 business days from 2026-09-12) — but he would still need to accrue 11 more hours of balance first.
- **Split the time off** into shorter blocks that fit within his 13-hour balance, each with the notice required for its length.

If you'd like, I can draft a ticket or email to Jonas explaining the shortfall and the compliant options.

**Answer**  
Tomas must first submit an International Remote Work request in Helios Workday.  
The request must be filed at least 20 business days before the intended start date, include the destination country (Brazil) and the exact dates, and obtain manager approval. After that, Global Mobility & Tax will review the request to determine if Brazil can be approved on a case‑by‑case basis, because Brazil is not on the list of automatically eligible countries.

**Why this is required**  
- The policy requires a formal request and a 20‑business‑day notice for all international remote work (POL‑INTL‑001 §4 Approval Workflow).  
- Brazil is not listed as an eligible country; any work there requires a special assessment by Global Mobility & Tax (POL‑INTL‑001 §3 Eligible Countries).  

**Citations**  
- POL‑INTL‑001 §4 Approval Workflow – “Employee submits an International Remote Work request in Helios Workday at least 20 business days before the intended start date… Manager approval… Global Mobility & Tax review.”  
- POL‑INTL‑001 §3 Eligible Countries – “Temporary international remote work is permitted only in countries where Helios has assessed the tax and permanent‑establishment risk… Work from any country not on this list is prohibited without a case‑by‑case assessment by Global Mobility & Tax.”

Questions about contractor compensation are handled by **Procurement**, not People Operations. (POL-BEN-001 §2 Employment Types)
